### Findings refused

- U37, U38, U31 · i "took the city" for baγ̇uba (Ming 下了): kept. Chinese 下 + a city is "take", the glossary already reads it so, and the narrative is not contradicted (U36 oroγ̇ulžu "made it submit" sits oddly after U31, but the n now flags the alternative). Not changed without a Ming 營.
- U19 · i "lives clenched in their teeth": kept; the Ming 刁 is "hold in the mouth" and the note says it is a literal reading, not an idiom.
- U26 · i "he would make it a law": kept as indirect speech (no quotation marks printed); hortative -je is carried by "would".
- U24 · n "the story of how Jirgo'adai got the name Jebe": kept; it points to the Secret History's own earlier text, not a modern translation. Cannot be checked against the files I may read.
- U34 · i dropping "own" of -ġen: kept; the n explains the reflexive and English "Whose word" carries the sense.
- U42 · l "returned-indeed": kept; follows the Ming 囘, with the n explaining the baγ̇u- reading.
- U1/U3 "-(n)i" and "-jin" labels: kept; they agree with the glossary entries.
- Lemma checks against the glossary: all agree (daγari-, qaγ̇ul-, tüši-, bügüd-, qoroqu-, nögči-, ketül-, ba for man-u) except the points above; new senses (qamsa-, ajala-, baγ̇ul-, Amui as a river) are left for the glosser to broaden.
